title: October 1st Was the Best Day of the Quarter (It Wasn't)
symptom: Finance's revenue dashboard shows October 1st at almost twice a normal day. The warehouse team says order volume that day looked ordinary, and no promotion ran. The dashboard reads the daily_sales table, which a nightly job fills.

goals.description: daily_sales holds each order exactly once, and no good rows were lost
daily_sales itself rejects the same order being loaded twice

evidence.description: what happened to the load for that day

options: A real sales spike that nobody noticed
The scheduled load finished but reported failure, it was re-run by hand, and because the load only appends and nothing enforces one row per order, the day was loaded twice
The dashboard's SUM query is wrong
Clock skew put September 30th's orders on October 1st

solution_commands: SELECT sale_date, count(*), sum(amount_cents) FROM daily_sales GROUP BY sale_date
SELECT * FROM daily_sales WHERE order_id IN (SELECT order_id FROM daily_sales GROUP BY order_id HAVING count(*) > 1) ORDER BY order_id LIMIT 4
DELETE FROM daily_sales WHERE rowid NOT IN (SELECT min(rowid) FROM daily_sales GROUP BY order_id)
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_daily_sales_order ON daily_sales(order_id)
debrief: Counting rows per day showed October 1st with twice the rows, not bigger orders. The job history told the story: the scheduled load inserted everything and then timed out notifying finance, so it was marked failed, and someone re-ran it at 09:41. The load is a plain INSERT, so the re-run appended a second copy, which the loaded_at timestamps on the duplicate rows confirm. Deleting all but the first copy of each order fixes the numbers; doing it inside BEGIN ... COMMIT lets you check the counts before it's final. The unique index is the real fix: with it, the re-run would have failed loudly instead of doubling revenue quietly. Better still, make the load idempotent (delete-then-insert for the day in one transaction, or INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), so re-running a job is always safe. See dataeng-incident-001 for the same bug in a warehouse.
